extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for the NIH Director's Pioneer Award (High‑Risk, High‑Reward applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application for the NIH Director's Pioneer Award: a single‑PI, High‑Risk, High‑Reward grant that supports creative investigators pursuing new scientific research directions and pioneering approaches to major biomedical, social science, or behavioral challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for scientists with outstanding records of creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: The award supports scientists with outstanding records of creativity pursuing new research directions to develop pioneering approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes an investigator's outstanding creativity and track record; applicants should demonstrate exceptional creativity in past work and propose novel directions. (Original phrasing: "scientists with outstanding records of creativity pursuing new research directions to develop pioneering approaches")

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on pioneering approaches to major challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should develop pioneering approaches to major challenges in biomedical, social science, and behavioral research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project scope must target major challenges within biomedical, social science, or behavioral research and propose pioneering (high‑risk/high‑reward) methodologies or concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must be a new scientific research direction
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed work must be a new scientific research direction for the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should describe a departure from the applicant's prior research trajectory — a genuinely new direction rather than incremental extension of ongoing work. (Original phrasing: "Must be new scientific research direction")

rubrics_metrics.name: Open to all career stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility is not limited by career stage; applicants at any career stage may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may be early‑career through senior investigators; indicate career stage as appropriate in the application. (Original phrasing: "Open to all career stages")

rubrics_metrics.name: Single PI only
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a single Principal Investigator may be named on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit multi‑PI or multiple PD/PI applications; all leadership must be centralized under one PI. (Original phrasing: "Single PI only")

rubrics_metrics.name: No preliminary data required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are not required to include preliminary data with their submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This award explicitly does not require preliminary data, enabling proposals that pursue high‑risk or novel ideas without supporting preliminary experiments. Use the narrative to justify feasibility and approach despite lack of preliminary data. (Original phrasing: "No preliminary data required")

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum research effort: 51% in first 3 years
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must commit a minimum of 51% research effort in the first 3 years of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and document percent effort so that at least 51% of the PI's effort is devoted to the award during the first three years; this is a binding award requirement. (Original phrasing: "Minimum of 51% research effort in first 3 years")

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Reference required (3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three Letters of Reference are required as part of the application package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange for exactly three reference letters to be submitted in accordance with application instructions and deadlines. (Original phrasing: "3 Letters of Reference required")

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: $700,000 direct costs/year up to 5 years
rubrics_metrics.description: The award provides $700,000 in direct costs per year for up to 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a budget request consistent with the $700,000/year direct cost cap and a project period not exceeding five years; follow NIH budget instructions for allowable costs. (Original phrasing: "$700,000 in direct costs per year for up to 5 years")

rubrics_metrics.name: Program context — High‑Risk, High‑Reward Research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pioneer Award is part of the High‑Risk, High‑Reward Research (HRHR) program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should align their proposals with the HRHR program's emphasis on high‑risk, high‑reward, and transformative research. Reference HRHR program goals where relevant.
